title: Hugging Face Microduck Teardown: 15 Motors, All Made by ROBOTIS (KOSDAQ: 108490)
content:
Hugging Face's Microduck is a 25 cm walking robot with 15 motors inside. According to a Korean brokerage report covered by Newsis, all 15 are actuators made by ROBOTIS, a KOSDAQ-listed company. Here is what is inside the robot, which parts have a confirmed listed maker, and what one robot is worth to that supplier.

Teardown reconstruction video (not a physical disassembly)

What is Microduck?

Microduck is a small bipedal robot released by Pollen Robotics, the robotics subsidiary of Hugging Face, the company best known for its open platform for sharing AI models.

  • Height: about 25 cm
  • List price: US$399 (about KRW 700,000 in Korea)
  • Form: two-legged walking robot
  • Pre-orders: about 15,000 units (Korea Investment & Securities analysis, reported by Newsis)

Microduck teardown: five kinds of parts

PartQtyListed makerEvidence
Servo actuator15ROBOTIS (KOSDAQ: 108490)Reported (Newsis, citing Korea Investment & Securities)

The parts list was compiled from public materials and the robot's software repository. We only name a maker when there is evidence; see our labeling rules.

1. Servo actuators (15) — ROBOTIS

A servo turns to an exact angle and holds it, which is why robots use them in their joints. When the motor, controller and gearbox are packed into one unit, the industry calls it an actuator.

Newsis reported on September 10, 2026 that Korea Investment & Securities analyst Choi Geon wrote that "Microduck carries 15 ROBOTIS actuators per unit." When we made the video we had only estimated, from size and layout, that the servos looked like the Dynamixel XL330 family. Dynamixel is ROBOTIS's flagship actuator brand. The report does not name the exact model.

2. Camera (1)

The round "face" holds a camera, the robot's eye.

3. ToF depth sensor (1)

A time-of-flight sensor fires light and times its return to measure distance. The camera sees what is there; the ToF sensor measures how far it is.

4. Motion sensors / IMU (2)

An IMU senses which way and how much the body is tilting, much like the balance organ in the human inner ear.

5. Microphone and speaker

For hearing and speaking.

Why does a 25 cm robot need 15 motors?

Fifteen motors in 25 cm means roughly one motor per joint. Standing on two legs is not a resting state: the body is constantly starting to fall and being caught again. The ankles and knees have to adjust force every moment, and that needs a separate motor for each joint. The two IMUs exist for the same reason: the robot must know which way it is tipping before it can decide which joint to push.

What is one Microduck worth to ROBOTIS?

More joints means more parts sold per robot. These are the figures from the Korea Investment & Securities analysis as reported by Newsis:

ItemFigureNote
Actuators per robot15Reported
Average selling price per actuatorabout KRW 20,000Analyst estimate
ROBOTIS revenue per robotabout KRW 300,00015 × KRW 20,000
At 15,000 pre-ordersabout KRW 4.5 billionAnalyst estimate
At the 50,000-unit sales targetabout KRW 15 billionAnalyst estimate

In a robot that sells for about KRW 700,000, the motors alone account for about KRW 300,000, over 40% of the retail price. That is the economics of walking robots in one line: cost scales with joint count × actuator price. The revenue figures are the analyst's estimates and depend on actual sales.

FAQ

Which listed company supplies Microduck?
ROBOTIS (KOSDAQ: 108490), for the 15 actuators, based on a Newsis report citing Korea Investment & Securities. Makers of the camera and sensors have not been confirmed.

How much does Microduck cost?
US$399 list price, about KRW 700,000 in Korea.

Who makes Microduck?
Pollen Robotics, Hugging Face's robotics subsidiary.

Is the video a real disassembly?
No. It is a reconstruction based on public information.

Summary

  • Hugging Face's Microduck: 25 cm bipedal robot, US$399
  • Inside: 15 servo actuators, camera, ToF sensor, 2 IMUs, microphone and speaker
  • The 15 actuators are made by ROBOTIS (KOSDAQ: 108490), per Newsis / Korea Investment & Securities
  • Estimated ROBOTIS revenue per robot: about KRW 300,000

Source: Newsis, September 10, 2026, report on Korea Investment & Securities' analysis of ROBOTIS (reporter Lee Ji-min). https://www.newsis.com/view/NISX20260910_0003783606
